items.item_text: Function as the primary support assistant for faculty and field groups. Also provide support for the Office of Academic Affairs/Dean of Faculty and serve as back-up to the Sr. Administrative Coordinator for department information, field group information, and administrative resources.
Provide day-to-day administrative and technical support to faculty members and field groups.
Assist Faculty in preparing reports, presentations, class materials, and other documents.
Perform data entry; Assist with setup and administration of distributing and collecting course evaluations

Provide faculty with technical and logistical assistance for virtual and in-person meetings, field trips, and on-campus events. Collect materials such as receipts, forms, and other documents as needed.
Place work orders for faculty to Facilities & Information Technology and follow-up as needed.
Learn and maintain knowledge of Field Groups to respond to questions from staff and students relating to Faculty and Field Groups.
Support tracking of faculty requests and with relevant staff and departments as needed.
Assist with Pitzer College committee minute-taking support

Provide support to the Office of Academic Affairs/Dean of Faculty Serve as a front-desk representative. Learn and maintain knowledge of academic affairs policies and procedures and answer questions about such policies and procedures. Assist in the maintenance of department website and faculty web pages as needed. Provide assistance to staff and administrators in the Dean of Faculty’s office as needed. Conduct research; develop draft documents; update lists and rosters. Under the supervision of the Sr. Administrative Coordination, assist in academic program-based support for offices and programs associated with the Dean of Faculty’s Office such as: Associate Dean of Faculty Programs First-Year Seminar Program Distinguished Academic Lectures Tutoring programs Summer Session

Assist in coordinating the administration, collection, and storage of course evaluations Serve as a primary contact for questions regarding course evaluations, Ensure compliance with processes and procedures for course evaluation distribution and access by faculty. Assist in generating reports for digital evaluation results and scanning paper evaluations for faculty.

Perform other duties as assigned such as, but not limited to Maintain inventory of supplies for the Academic Affairs Office. Assist with faculty supply orders and reception of supplies. Keep copy rooms stocked and maintain copy machines. Assist with room access for faculty and staff. Coordinate projects and tasks with student assistants. Backup support for budget and finance tasks for faculty.
Ability to maintain strict confidentiality and exercise a very high degree of independent judgment, tact, and discretion in the execution of assigned responsibilities.
Ability to prioritize, organize large volumes of paperwork and emails, use time efficiently and manage multiple tasks to satisfy expectations and tight deadlines.
Ability to switch between tasks quickly while maintaining workflow and attention to detail in a busy office environment.
Adapts to changes in the work environment, manages competing demands and deals with frequent change, interruptions, delays or unexpected events with aplomb.
Ability to independently conduct research and produce complex reports and presentations.
Superior people skills, a customer service attitude, teamwork skills, and the ability to interact well in a culturally diverse work environment.

Excellent word processing skills. Advanced-level skills with the full Microsoft Office suite and Adobe Acrobat. Knowledge of (or ability to quickly learn) data management systems and online job application systems (in use: People Admin).

Strong editing and proofing skills in English. Writes English with attention to spelling, grammar, accuracy and the needs of the target audience; presents numerical data effectively; and uses various mediums of communication effectively (e.g. emails, memos, reports, etc.).
Demonstrates initiative in anticipating schedules and needs to move projects forward.
Excellent calendar management skills, including the coordination of complex meetings.
Sit and operate a computer for prolonged periods of time.
Mobility to work in a standard office setting and use standard office equipment.
Must be able to communicate in person and over the telephone.
Must be able to read printed materials and a computer screen.
Must be able to assist with the set-up and tear-down of event tables, signage and other materials, including reaching overhead, grasping, pulling, pushing, stooping, bending, and twisting.
Cover Letter : Indicate your reason for interest in this position, describe how your qualifications make you an ideal candidate, and explain which of Pitzer’s core values best relates to your own.
Resume : List relevant qualifications and dates of experience.

Professional References : References will be contacted for select applicants and advance notice will be provided. Provide the names of at least three (3) individuals who can speak to your professional qualifications. Include their business titles, contact information and an indication of how you are acquainted with them (e.g., former supervisor, coworker, etc.).
Campus Security Authority Reporter (CSA ): Employees responsible for reporting crimes that are disclosed to them, so that crime statistics reporting is as accurate as possible.

Federal Educational Rights and Privacy Act Reporter (FERPA) : Employees with access to student records and information must adhere to the privacy protection requirements under FERPA, which restricts what student information may be disclosed and to whom.
Mandatory Reporter : Employees who have frequent contact with children are required to report all known or suspected cases of child abuse or neglect.

Responsible Employee : Any employee who has the authority to take action to redress sexual violence, who has been given the duty of reporting incidents of sexual violence or any other misconduct by students to the Title IX Coordinator or other appropriate School designee; or whom a student could reasonably believe has this authority or duty.
